  "summary": "This single-page, unattributed typewritten submission provides 14 numbered answers to a committee questionnaire on election expenses. The respondent rejects or declines to endorse some proposed arrangements, including subsidies, while suggesting that the State could print and distribute specified quantities of campaign materials—posters, leaflets, manifestoes, and voters’ slips—to candidates under conditions ensuring their proper use.\n\nThe response argues that political parties should be legally required to maintain accounts open to public scrutiny and hold regular internal elections. It rejects statutory ceilings on campaign expenditure, claiming that such limits encourage dishonest returns and that those intent on cheating will evade the law. It also addresses compulsory voting and publicly provided transport, warning that restricting candidate-provided transport could create incentives to offer transport in exchange for votes.
